newsitem.title: UK: Kenya denies UN report on counterfeit dollars.
newsitem.headline: Kenya denies UN report on counterfeit dollars.

text.p: Kenya's finance minister on Thursday dismissed a United Nations report saying Rwandan Hutu rebels based in his country were printing counterfeit U.S. dollars to finance fighting in Zaire and Rwanda.
"It is completely outrageous," Musalia Mudavadi told a news conference in London.
"We don't have any such printing press for counterfeit currency in Kenya, neither are we party to any scheme or any organisation which might be financing any activities in the Great Lakes region."
Reuters on Tuesday obtained a report prepared for the Security Council by a four-man commission of inquiry saying counterfeit money was being used to buy arms from Europe and South Africa.
Mudavadi, in London to discuss economic cooperation with ministers from Uganda and Tanzania, said it was in Kenya's interests that conflict in the Great Lakes region should stop immediately.
He said his country had pursued diplomatic initiatives to end the fighting.
Repeating that there were no counterfeiters in Kenya, Mudavadi said anyone accepting bogus U.S. currency for arms "must be fools".
"If there was any such thing, I think those people should be treated as common criminals, and not people with any support from the government of Kenya," he added.

Tanzanian Foreign Minister Jakaya Kikwete told the news conference at the Commonwealth Secretariat that he would prefer to see an all-African force, rather than one with troops from outside the continent, intervening in eastern Zaire to protect refugees there.
"If it is going to be an all-African force, that is better, but if it is going to be an international force including the Africans, that would be acceptable," he said.
Kikwete said it was essential to protect the territorial integrity of Zaire. In return Zaire must accept as its citizens all the people of the Kivu region where fighting has been taking place.
"If you accept the territory, accept the people within that territory. Don't say "I want this piece of land, but I don't want you'," he said.
